thesis: Innventure identifies technologies inside large corporations, then creates and operates new companies to commercialize them. The public ticker consolidates several operating companies, led today by Accelsius (two-phase liquid cooling for AI and high-performance computing), with AeroFlexx (flexible packaging) and Refinity (plastics/olefins) earlier in the life cycle. PureCycle was an earlier Innventure company that is now a separate public equity. At the parent, reported revenue is still very small and losses are large while the subsidiaries raise capital and try to scale.
why_market_wrong: The market may be pricing INV as a thin, cash-burning holding company rather than as a claim on Accelsius's cooling franchise if two-phase cooling becomes required as chip power rises. The predictive attribute is commercial adoption of Accelsius systems at hyperscalers and high-density sites, not near-term consolidated earnings. Inefficiency comes from complexity: multi-entity capital structure, preferreds and noncontrolling interests, and a short public history after the Learn CW business combination.
